name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
summary: A neurodevelopmental condition marked by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsiveness.

name: Allergic diseases (asthma, atopic dermatitis, food allergy)
summary: Conditions in which the immune system overreacts to harmless substances such as foods and environmental allergens.

name: Alzheimer's disease
summary: The most common form of dementia, marked by memory loss and gradual decline in thinking.

name: Anorexia nervosa
summary: An eating disorder involving severe food restriction and low body weight.

name: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea
summary: Diarrhea that develops during or after a course of antibiotics.

name: Antibiotic resistance
summary: When gut bacteria stop responding to antibiotics, which can make infections harder to treat.

name: Antidepressants
summary: Medicines for depression, including SSRIs, whose effects on gut bacteria are only starting to be studied in humans.

name: Anxiety
summary: Persistent, excessive worry and fear that can escalate into panic attacks, a racing heart and sweating.

name: Anxiety disorders
summary: Conditions marked by excessive, persistent worry or fear.

name: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
summary: A neurodevelopmental condition marked by differences in social communication and by restricted or repetitive behavior, often with gut symptoms.

name: Bifidobacterium
summary: A group of gut bacteria generally considered beneficial, and a common ingredient in probiotics.

name: Bile acids
summary: Digestive molecules that gut microbes modify.

name: Bipolar Disorder
summary: A mental health condition that causes extreme shifts in mood, energy, and activity levels, alternating between periods of high energy (mania or hypomania) and low mood (depression)

name: Depression
summary: A common mental health condition that affects how you feel, think and function each day which can cause ongoing sadness, low energy and loss of interest in things you once enjoyed.

name: Dietary fiber
summary: Diet-based interventions that change what gut microbes have available to ferment.

name: Faecalibacterium
summary: A butyrate-producing gut bacterium that is often found at lower levels in people with inflammatory, metabolic, and mood conditions.

name: Fermented foods
summary: Foods made through microbial growth, such as yoghurt, kefir, sauerkraut and kombucha.

name: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT)
summary: Transferring stool from a screened donor to restore a healthier gut microbial community.

name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
summary: A common disorder of gut-brain interaction with abdominal pain and altered bowel habits.

name: Infectious diseases
summary: Illnesses caused by bacteria, viruses, or other microbes, such as gut, respiratory, and bloodstream infections.

name: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
summary: A group of long-term inflammatory conditions of the gut, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

name: Lactic acid bacteria
summary: A group of beneficial, Gram-positive, and acid-tolerant microorganisms that convert sugars into lactic acid through fermentation, playing a key role in food preservation, dairy production, and human gut health.

name: Mediterranean eiet
summary: A heart-healthy, plant-based eating pattern inspired by the traditional foods of countries bordering the Mediterranean Sea, focusing on daily vegetables, fruits, whole grains, beans, nuts, and extra-virgin olive oil while limiting red meat and processed foods

name: Metformin
summary: A widely prescribed diabetes drug that changes the mix of bacteria in the gut.

name: Microbial diversity
summary: The number and balance of different microbes in the gut.

name: Multiple sclerosis
summary: A long-term autoimmune disease in which the immune system damages nerve fibres in the brain and spinal cord.

name: MyD88 innate immune signaling
summary: MyD88 is a protein that relays signals from immune receptors that sense microbes, linking the gut microbiota to immune responses.

name: NSAIDs
summary: Common anti-inflammatory painkillers, such as ibuprofen and aspirin, that can alter gut bacteria.

name: Parkinson's disease
summary: A brain disease that causes movement problems such as tremor and stiffness, often preceded by gut symptoms.

name: Postbiotics
summary: Preparations of deliberately inactivated microbes or their parts that may give a health benefit.

name: Prebiotics
summary: Substrates that are selectively used by host microorganisms.

name: Prevotella
summary: A group of gut bacteria that tends to become more common with fiber-rich, plant-based diets.

name: Probiotics
summary: Live microorganisms given to confer a health benefit.

name: Proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs)
summary: Acid-reducing drugs that are linked to changes in gut bacteria, including bacteria moving from the upper to the lower gut.

name: Psychotropic medications
summary: Drugs used to treat mental health conditions, such as mood stabilizers and antipsychotics.

name: Recurrent C. difficile infection
summary: C. difficile infection that returns after treatment.

name: Short-chain fatty acids
summary: Metabolites produced when gut bacteria ferment fiber.

name: Schizophrenia
summary: A chronic, severe brain disorder characterized by a disruption in thought processes, perceptions, and emotions, causing individuals to lose touch with reality through symptoms like hallucinations and delusions.

name: Statins
summary: Cholesterol-lowering drugs that have been linked to shifts in gut bacteria.

name: Sulfate-reducing bacteria
summary: Gut bacteria such as Bilophila and Desulfovibrio that have been linked to inflammation.

name: Synbiotics
summary: Products that combine live beneficial microbes with a food ingredient that feeds them.

name: Systemic inflammation
summary: Low-grade body-wide immune activation, often measured by blood markers such as CRP and IL-6, that may influence mood and brain function.

name: Type 1 diabetes
summary: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system destroys the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas.

name: Type 2 diabetes
summary: A long-term condition in which blood sugar stays too high because the body doesn't use insulin well.

name: Ulcerative colitis
summary: A form of inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colon.

name: Whole diet interventions
summary: Changes to overall eating patterns, rather than single supplements, aimed at improving health through the gut microbiome.
